title: ProjectorClear
question: How does a cinema projector work?
hook: A Maltese cross that stops the film 24 times a second, a shutter that flashes every frame twice, and a chip with 9 million tilting mirrors. Step into the booth and see how a cinema throws a picture 30 metres onto a wall.

explainer.title: Film stops, flashes, then jumps
explainer.text: A 35 mm projector pulls film from a platter through a gate. A Maltese cross turns a steady spin into a quarter-turn jerk: the film moves one frame in about 10 ms, then stands still for 31 ms. A two-bladed shutter hides the jump and flashes each frame twice, so 24 frames become 48 flashes, fast enough that the flicker disappears.

explainer.title: Nine million mirrors per colour
explainer.text: A digital cinema projector splits lamp or laser light into red, green and blue, one DLP chip each. A 4K chip has 4096 × 2160 mirrors about 7.5 µm apart that tilt ±12°. Grey comes from timing: each mirror flips on and off thousands of times a second, and your eye averages the flashes.

explainer.title: The lens sets the size, the screen sets the brightness
explainer.text: Picture width = throw × chip width ÷ focal length. Tilting a high projector makes a keystone, so cinemas use lens shift. The DCI standard asks for 14 fL (48 cd/m²); a silver screen is about 2.4× brighter straight on but dim from the side.

explainer.title: 3D is two films sharing one screen
explainer.text: One projector flashes left and right pictures 144 times a second. Polarised, active-shutter or colour-filter glasses let each eye see only its own picture. Each eye gets its picture half the time, and filters swallow more, so roughly a fifth of the light arrives.

explainer.title: A film in files, locked with a key
explainer.text: Films arrive as a DCP: JPEG 2000 frames at up to 250 Mbit/s, roughly 150 to 250 GB for a feature, by drive, internet or satellite (India's UFO Moviez and Qube pioneered satellite delivery). The files are encrypted and only play when a KDM key, made for that one server, is valid.

explainer.title: Bigger, faster, brighter
explainer.text: IMAX runs 70 mm film sideways, 15 perforations a frame, about ten times the area of 35 mm, and now uses twin lasers. Some films tried 48 or 120 fps. LED screens such as Samsung Onyx (2017) need no projector at all, while India's single screens give way to multiplexes.

concepts.def: A pin wheel and slotted Maltese cross that turn smooth rotation into quick quarter-turn steps.
A spinning bladed disc that blocks light while the film moves and flashes each frame, usually twice.
The flash rate above which light looks steady; at cinema brightness roughly 40 to 50 Hz.
A digital micromirror device: a chip of millions of hinged mirrors, one per pixel, tilting on or off.
Making in-between brightness by switching fully on and off and varying the on time.
Distance to the screen divided by picture width, set by the lens focal length.
A unit of screen brightness; the DCI standard is 14 fL, or 48 cd/m².
How much brighter a screen looks straight on than matte white; silver is about 2.4.
The Digital Cinema Package of encrypted files, and the Key Delivery Message that unlocks it for one server and time window.
